identity.description: Apify is a web scraping and browser automation platform. Developers build and run cloud programs called Actors and use the Apify REST API to run them and access datasets, key-value stores and request queues.
identity.identity_notes: docs.apify.com documents the Apify platform; apify.com hosts the Apify Store and the Apify MCP server docs. This matches the named app (Apify, Data/SEO/Scraping category).

auth.oauth_flows: OAuth is documented for the hosted MCP server connection (browser sign-in on first connection). No third-party OAuth app registration for the REST API was found; the OAuth docs page returned 404.
auth.scopes_notes: Scoped tokens are mentioned for scheduling Actors and Tasks. Full scope list not established.

access.production_restrictions: Free plan has usage limits: free users are blocked until the next billing cycle when usage runs out; paid users can continue with overage. Free-plan Apify Proxy cannot be used by external clients.

read_ops: Get/list Actors, runs, builds, tasks, schedules, webhooks
Read datasets, key-value stores and request queues
write_ops: Run an Actor (POST to the Run Actor endpoint)
api.rate_limits: Global limit 250,000 requests per minute; default 60 requests per second per resource, higher for certain endpoints; 429 responses call for exponential backoff.
api.limitations: Webhook action is limited to a POST HTTP request to a URL. Python client existence not verified. Exact write verbs for tasks/schedules/storage not verified on fetched pages.

open_questions: Whether a Python client exists (not verified on fetched pages; the JS client page does not mention one).
Whether third-party OAuth app registration for the REST API exists (OAuth docs page at docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/oauth returned 404).
Trial availability and sandbox: not stated on fetched pages.
Exact HTTP write verbs for tasks, schedules, webhooks and storage not verified.

Community MCP servers: the only community listing found is a copy of the official server description (apify.com/securitybyobscurity/apify-mcp-server). No independent implementation found; the Tester MCP Client is a UI, not a server, and its maintainer status is unclear. The apify.com pricing page also returned 404 for one fetch; free-plan facts came from the search-retrieved pricing page.

assessment.approach: Wrap/benchmark vendor's official MCP server; add managed auth
rationale: Self-serve test credentials (free self serve) and a documented CLI/library/REST interface.
